paper_id: Zheng et al. - 2018 - Combating Cross-Technology Interference for Robust Wireless Sensing with COTS WiFi
title: Combating Cross-Technology Interference for Robust Wireless Sensing with COTS WiFi
motivation: WiFi sensing suffers severe CTI from Bluetooth/ZigBee/microwave, degrading CSI and sensing performance, yet this is surprisingly overlooked
problem_framing: Detect per-CSI interference, identify distorted subcarriers, and repair them via frequency-domain interpolation
key_insight: Non-WiFi devices occupy only narrow instant bandwidth, affecting specific subcarriers → can identify and interpolate
method_signature: Cyclostationarity-based RFI detection + linear interpolation of distorted subcarriers
evaluation_criteria: >30% performance gain on human detection; detection time 1.5s/500 samples; >90% TP rate for different CTI types
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Temporal filters fail on persistent CTI, attenuate motion-induced dynamics, and require sequential data
evidence_for_taste: pose severe impacts on CSI measurements
thinking_moves: 从field遗漏的critical issue出发: 证明问题存在且严重
借鉴pilot-aided OFDM信道估计思想做interpolation
cyclostationarity理论从通信检测迁移到CSI感知
强调与现有分类器orthogonal、可叠加
